content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper the authors propose a method to perform federated learning in the presence of heterogeneous (non-iid) data across the participating clients. The authors adapt an approach earlier used to arrest the forgetting effect widely known in the context of continual learning to the federated learning setting and show improvement over FedAVG method. The authors attempt to quantify the "client forgetting" at each participant and use it find insights about the benefits of the proposed approach.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper is well written in terms of describing the problem set-up, related art on continual learning and model drift in federated learning. The paper clearly describes the motivation to use the proposed approach and provides empirical evidence of the benefits of using this approach as opposed to the classic FedAVG algorithm.  It also discusses the use of BN and GN and its implications on the accuracy.

The main drawback of the paper is the lack of empirical comparison with any of the large number of earlier approaches for solving the problem of non-IID federated learning (see below for a few references). Even though the authors talk about the disadvantages of them in a qualitative and cursory manner, there are no experiments defined to quantify the trade-offs. 

[1]. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231221013254
[2]. https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/papers/Gao_FedDC_Federated_Learning_With_Non-IID_Data_via_Local_Drift_Decoupling_CVPR_2022_paper.pdf
[3]. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.06440.pdf
[4]. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.03452.pdf

I have some other concerns/questions on the paper below..

1) I would like to see the sensitivity of the proposed algorithm with the value of local epochs(E)  as studied in FedAVG paper
2) In most of the practical cases, the "other" classes for a client will not be completely absent but will have fewer examples (samples) for them as opposed to their majority labels. How do you decide which classes to exclude in such cases? In other words, is there a threshold used to decide to skip the classes in computing trudged CE?
3) Is there a consistent winner between GN and BN while using TCE? It will be nice to see some insights and reasoning on that.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Cleary written and easy to follow
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: To overcome "cateastropic forgetting" phenomenon in non i.i.d Federated Learning, authors propose to use a truncated cross entropy loss function to prevent updating/training local model on classes not present in the local dataset. Authors show that this simple modification can show singinicant improvement upon final accuracy. They perform several ablation experiments on different FL settings.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1: The idea is simple and seems effective, which shows siginificant improvement on final accuracy in CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 non-iid datasets.

Weakness:

1: The truncated cross entropy loss function is not novel. As stated in paper, "For the supervised continual learning setting Caccia et al. (2022); Ahn et al. (2021) proposed a modification of the standard cross entropy objective function that truncates the softmax denominator, removing terms corresponding to classes from old tasks." This makes this paper a straight forward application of such idea on FL tasks.

2: In many realistic non-iid settings, most of classes will be present in every clients but with sifinicantly different distribution. I am not sure whether the current method can still show large improvement in the final accuracy.

3: Authors should also experiment on applying TCE on other FL algorithms, such as FedProx, to give a more comprehensive picture.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity and Quality:

Overall good.

Novelty:

I am a little concern about the novelty as stated above.

Reproducibility:

Seems to be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: I recommend weak reject mainly due to novelty concern. But I am willing to change my score if other reviewers find it still is a good contribution to the FL research.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
Summary: 
- Issue: Heterogeneity of data across clients in FL.
- Proposed method: Using truncated cross-entropy objective on a per-client basis.
- Experiment: 1) Model non-iid clients with Dirichlet distribution parameterized 2) Tested on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and FMNIST with ResNet 18. 3) Comparison with a simple baseline. 4) Ablation study with different normalization methods, learning rates, heterogeneity levels, and factions of participating clients.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pro: 
- This paper formulates the non-iid problem in FL from an interesting angle – client forgetting. 
- The proposed method is easy to implement. 

Cons:
- Overall, the paper is not well-written and well-prepared. Several obvious grammar issues should be corrected
- The truncated cross-entropy method was actually used in previous works, including: 

[1] Diao, Enmao, Jie Ding, and Vahid Tarokh. "HeteroFL: Computation and communication efficient federated learning for heterogeneous clients." ICLR 2021.

[2] Hong, Junyuan, et al. "Efficient Split-Mix Federated Learning for On-Demand and In-Situ Customization." ICLR 2022.

- Although the authors showed that the proposed methods could work on their settings, a deeper understanding of why truncated cross-entropy can help client forgetting is important for the papers publishing on top ML venues
- The experiments lack sufficient comparison with the existing SOTA solutions for data heterogeneity issues in FL.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
- This paper proposes a simple modification of cross-entropy loss as a local objective function on remote clients, which prevents diverging updates due to the heterogeneous local data.
- This paper demonstrates that the proposed algorithm improves typical cross-entropy loss on multiple image classification benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strong points

- This paper observes empirically that excluding the classifier weights of the unseen classes for local training prevents the learned classifier from being biased on skewed classes which exist in local data.

### Weak points

- Writing is poor and not easy to follow, overall statements are vague, missing discussions.
    - In Section 2, a paragraph about normalization techniques in federated learning is not actually related to this work.
    - In the caption of Figure 1,  authors should present any evidence to support the claim that “a global model with knowledge of all classes is sent to clients which increase loss on their local data distribution”. In my opinion, [1] could be evidence of this statement.
- This paper only compares the proposed method with conventional cross-entropy loss. Authors should compare the proposed method with other SOTA federated learning algorithms that handle data heterogeneity over clients.
- Authors should evaluate the proposed method on other federated learning frameworks such as FedADAM [2], FedDYN [3], and SCAFFOLD [4].
- The performance becomes trivial either when the participation rate is high or when data heterogeneity becomes low (a large value of alpha).
- The idea of excluding parameters of seen classes is not novel in continual learning. Simply adopting this approach in federated learning lacks novelty.

### Questions

- Why two different normalization techniques (group normalization and batch normalization) are evaluated in the main table? These normalization techniques are orthogonal with the proposed loss function.


### References

[1]  C. Xu et al., Acceleration of Federated Learning with Alleviated Forgetting in Local Training, ICLR, 2022

[2] S.J. Reddi et al., Adaptive Federated Optimization, ICLR, 2021

[3] D.A.E. Acar et al., Federated Learning Based on Dynamic Regularization, ICLR, 2021

[4] S.P. Karimireddy et al., SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Clarity and quality: Writing is poor and needs to be improved
- Novelty: The proposed method is not novel.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this paper lacks novelty and requires more comprehensive experiments to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
